# Interactive Text-to-SQL via Expected Information Gain for Disambiguation

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#sql-eig)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.06467v1) · arXiv:2507.06467v1, 9 July 2025; manuscript venue/artifact fields remain placeholders

**Reading coverage:** All 13 PDF pages: Sections 1-7, Theorem 3.2 and proof, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-4, Figures 1-5/captions and references. Table 1 and adjacent claims visually checked. No supplement appended.

## Research question

Choose informative clarifications from alternative SQL interpretations rather than fixing a query component order.

## Method

Maintains weighted SQL candidates, extracts branching variables, selects expected entropy reduction and filters candidates using user answers. The method depends on candidate completeness and usable probabilities.

## Evaluation

AmbiQT uses gold-based simulated answers. Spider evaluation selects 290 cases whose most likely candidate has probability below 0.7; additional Spider2 results are reported. No real-user study is described.

## What the results support

Table 1 reports 76.6% execution and 38.3% exact match on the selected Spider subset, versus 73.4% and 33.8% for information gain. Gains compare interaction policies over a preselected candidate space.

## Limits and qualifications

The prose gives inconsistent exact-match baselines (21.0 versus 33.8 in Table 1). Stepwise entropy maximization does not by itself establish optimal whole-dialogue effort. User noise, missing intended candidates and concrete artifact/experiment configurations remain unresolved.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A principled clarification heuristic whose empirical and optimality claims require the stated candidate and simulator assumptions.
